script.base: Closing line is CAR +3, total 47.5, outdoors (open and rest/travel not in the pack). Books expect Dallas to lead a one-score game, implied DAL 25.2 / CAR 22.2. Carolina is not a 3.5-point dog, so the base is not a pass-chase: with Chuba Hubbard out, Rico Dowdle keeps the Panthers on the ground in a close game, while Dallas, missing CeeDee Lamb and KaVontae Turpin, still has to throw to move the ball to Jake Ferguson (30 targets, 171 yards, only 79 air yards in weeks 3-5) and George Pickens, with Javonte Williams (46 carries, 296 yards in those three games) closing if Dallas leads late.
script.flip1: Dallas gets up by two scores early, runs the clock through Williams, and Carolina abandons the run. Dowdle's carries die, Bryce Young is forced into a Dallas blitz look he has handled poorly (CAR EPA/db -0.23 vs blitz vs 0.02 vs none; DAL blitz 23%), and Ferguson/Pickens target volume rises only if the lead is not already safe.
script.flip2: Carolina leads or the game outscores a 47.5 total. Both quarterbacks throw, Tetairoa McMillan (24 targets, 304 air yards in weeks 3-5) and Pickens become the live overs, and both lead backs lose late carries. Unsaved outdoor weather is the other flip: wind 15-plus would cut deep yards and push both offenses toward the run and Ferguson's short area.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report, not the 90-minute inactives. CAR RB Chuba Hubbard Out (calf): Dowdle is next man up. Weeks 3-5 he already had 42 carries/268 yards while Hubbard had 27/122 and Trevor Etienne 11/55, so the vacated ~9 Hubbard carries per game should land mostly on Dowdle, with Etienne as the change-of-pace, not the lead. CAR T Taylor Moton Out (elbow) and DT Tershawn Wharton Out (toe): Carolina's own rush efficiency should fall, and Dallas's run path gets a bit softer. CAR CBs Akayleb Evans Out, Mike Jackson and Chau Smith-Wade Questionable: secondary depletion helps Pickens/Ferguson if the questionable corners sit. CAR WR Jalen Coker and TE Ja'Tavion Sanders Questionable: if they sit, McMillan and Tommy Tremble gain; not assumed. DAL WR CeeDee Lamb Out (ankle) and KaVontae Turpin Out (foot): target vacuum toward Ferguson (already the leader at 30 targets), Pickens (24 targets/259 yards/309 air), Jalen Tolbert (13/85), and Ryan Flournoy (14/149, no prop listed). DAL RB Miles Sanders Out (knee): Williams is the bellcow; Jaydon Blue (4 carries, 7 yards in the recent window) is not the absorber. DAL G Tyler Booker Out, G Tyler Smith and T Ajani Cornelius Questionable: Dallas interior/tackle health is a real rush-efficiency drag. DAL LB Jack Sanborn Out (concussion) helps Carolina TE/RB catches. DAL CBs Trevon Diggs, DaRon Bland, and Caelen Carson all Questionable, so McMillan's matchup is not locked.

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone rates are not in the pack, so no shell is assigned. Only location splits and blitz rates are known.
matchup.pressure: CAR blitzes 21%; Dallas EPA/db is 0.09 when blitzed vs 0.25 when not, so pressure is not the Cowboys' problem and a low blitz rate leaves the intermediate game intact for Ferguson. DAL blitzes 23%; Carolina EPA/db is -0.23 when blitzed vs 0.02 when not, so a blitz-heavy Dallas plan would kill McMillan deep shots and push Young to checkdowns (Dowdle/Tremble), but 23% is not a blitz identity.
matchup.bleeds: CAR allows 4.75 YPC and 13 runs of 10-plus in 5 games; pass YPA left 7.29 (66 att), middle 9.71 (35), right 4.65 (51); 14 passes of 20-plus for 157 yards. DAL allows 4.67 YPC and 21 runs of 10-plus; pass YPA left 9.5 (72), middle 11.77 (30), right 6.19 (78); 18 passes of 20-plus for 190 yards. Carolina's bleed is the middle, not the right sideline. Dallas's bleed is the middle and explosives, plus a run defense that does not stonewall.
matchup.overlap: Ferguson is the primary Dallas target (30 targets, 2.6 air yards per target) into the only soft CAR slice (middle 9.71 YPA). That is the core overlap. Pickens' 309 air yards would need explosives CAR has allowed only 14 times in 5 games, and the right side (4.65 YPA) is a bad guess without alignment. Dowdle's carry role overlaps a Dallas front that has allowed 21 runs of 10-plus and 4.67 YPC, not a stuffed box. McMillan (304 air yards) overlaps Dallas's middle 11.77 and 18 explosives, but Young-vs-blitz and three questionable Dallas corners make it unresolved, so he is not a leg.

form: Avoid season averages; weeks 3-5 are the role window. Dowdle 42/268 rush and 6 targets/34 yards; the three-game rush split that sums to 268 is 30, 32, 206, and the older last4 game is the 9. Etienne's weeks 3-5 sum to 55, matching 0, 33, 22, with a 4 outside that window. Williams weeks 3-5 sum to 296, matching 76, 85, 135 (the 97 is the older last4 game); receiving last4 33, 16, 15, 4 is fading. Ferguson last4 receiving 78, 82, 40, 49 on a 57-yard weeks 3-5 average. Pickens last4 68, 68, 134, 57: only the 134 clears 68.5, so the yardage is explosive-inflated. McMillan last4 100, 48, 62, 73 sits on 68.5. Tolbert 16, 24, 61, 0 and Hunter Renfrow 48, 6, 10, 7 are too spiky. Blue has one listed game at 7 rush yards.

Lamb Out and Turpin Out: Pickens 68.5, Ferguson 49.5, Tolbert 16.5; Flournoy has targets (14/149) but no listed prop. Wharton and Moton are trench outs, not skill sleepers. Moton's absence cannot crater efficiency all the way under 3 yards per carry.
edge_players.kills_it: Carolina trails by 14-plus and abandons the run; Etienne and Young siphon the Hubbard leftovers; a loaded box plus Moton out produces another 9-yard floor; or Hubbard is a surprise active. The 206-yard game is one explosive and is not the case.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because 30.5 was Dowdle's ordinary game, not a soft one: weeks 3-5 were 30, 32, and a single 206-yard explosion that will not travel. Moton is out, so the 6.4 YPC falls, Dallas loads the box with Lamb and Turpin gone, and a two-score deficit makes Young abandon the run the way a trailing back's line dies. Etienne (11 carries, 55 yards in that window) takes the Hubbard leftovers and Dowdle finishes in the 9-to-30 band. Ferguson loses the same day if the 40 and 49 are the real usage, Dallas runs the clock through Williams (last4 rush 97, 76, 85, 135, with the recent three backing out to 76, 85, 135), and Carolina sits on the middle. No saved price also means these may have been medians, not markets.
slip_story: One competitive-game usage story, not a shootout and not a clock-kill stack: Dowdle rush over survives the base one-score script and the Carolina-leads flip, and is tagged script-dependent on flip1; Ferguson receiving over is the same close-game pass volume with Lamb and Turpin out, and is tagged script-dependent on a Dallas blowout. They do not need opposite scripts. Two legs, no touchdowns, one market per player, no depth receiver. Williams rush over 85.5 was the other sleeper and was dropped: the weeks 3-5 split (76, 85, 135) sits on the 85.5 line, Booker is out, and a loaded box with Lamb out is a stronger counter than the Sanders-out carry bump.
